assumptions: All figures are in today's dollars. That is what money buys now.

Stocks grow 5.0% a year above inflation on average, and bonds 1.8%. Some years are good and some are bad. These are planning figures, not a forecast. They stay fixed, so every plan faces the same markets. To see a bad stretch, try 'markets fall 30%'.
A market test is one made-up run of the markets, year by year. We test many of them. 'Safe in 90 of 100 market tests' means your money lasts in 90 of every 100.

Until you retire you save about $6,362 a year. $5,900 goes into a 401(k) or IRA: that is assumed, 10% of pay. $462 is take-home pay left after spending, which the plan assumes you save. If that is wrong, change 'Yearly saving' in your answers.
Pay stays the same until you retire. The plan counts no raises, since they are not certain. If your pay changes, update it in your answers.

Social Security is a rough guess from today's pay. We count work from about 22 until you retire. Missing years under 35 count as zero. Your own figure is at ssa.gov/myaccount. Your answers show $28,200 a year from 67. This plan starts it at 70. That pays about $35,000 a year.
If you retire before 65, health cover costs about $10,000 a person a year until Medicare starts. This is a guess. Other health costs follow US government figures by age.

Tax uses 2027 federal rates, the standard deduction and your state's rates. While you work, 401(k) saving lowers your taxable pay. In retirement we count 85% of Social Security as taxed. That is the most the law allows, so tax may run a little high.
The plan runs to age 94. There is about a 1 in 4 chance that you will live that long. This comes from a US life table. People with more money often live longer.

headline: You can count on $33,700 a year, about your needs. Little is left for wants. That is less than your Social Security of $35,000 a year. It starts at 70 in this plan.
headline_why: That is because savings must cover the years before it starts and health costs come on top.

rows.title: A poor first decade
rows.what: Stocks earn 5 points a year less than usual for the first 10 years of your retirement.
rows.label: Stocks do badly for 10 years
rows.short: Savings run out at 89. You would cut about $4,000 a year for 5 years. Your needs stay paid in 92 of 100 market tests.
rows.sentence: Your $34,000 a year still lasts in most market tests. In the worst 1 in 10, savings run out at 89. You would then cut about $4,000 a year for 5 years. Your needs stay paid in 92 of 100 market tests.

rows.title: Higher inflation
rows.what: Prices rise 1.5 points a year faster than we assume for 10 years. Savings earn that much less.
rows.label: Prices rise faster for 10 years
rows.sentence: Your needs would go unpaid in 12 of 100 market tests. You could count on about $33,000 a year, down from $34,000.

rows.title: Living to 100

rows.short: Savings run out at 94. You would cut about $4,000 a year for 6 years. Your needs stay paid in 92 of 100 market tests.

stresses.line: The biggest risk: prices rise faster for 10 years. You could count on $32,800 a year, and your needs are paid in 88 of 100 market tests.
